name: Peter Thiel
role: German-American entrepreneur and investor (PayPal, Palantir, Founders Fund) and Republican donor
summary: Thiel began as a libertarian who funded Ron Paul and seasteading, wrote in 2009 that freedom and democracy are no longer compatible, and has since moved toward a nationalist, pro-Trump position focused on technological stagnation, hostility to China and skepticism of global governance. He favours dynamism, risk-taking and technological acceleration, opposes regulatory caution and environmentalism, and frames one-world government as a spiritual and political danger. He is openly gay, supports marriage equality and says culture-war issues distract from economic decline.

sources.usedFor: Report on his Antichrist lectures: environmentalism and regulation as end-times politics.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Says he stands against confiscatory taxes and gave $3 million in Dec 2025 to fight a proposed California billionaire wealth tax.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Laments that atoms are regulated and bits are not, and wants the FDA and nuclear regulation loosened; he backs state action against Google and China, but not general corporate regulation.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Counts imprisonment for even mild drug use among rights violations and backed a marijuana legalisation effort.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Started a student paper that helped undo Stanford speech codes and consistently opposes silencing heterodox speech.

state-harmful.rationale: Prefers a small state (Singapore as an example, between France and Somalia) rather than none; says he wants less government but not none.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Gave to AFER and to defeat Minnesota's 2012 marriage ban, and is openly gay.

gradual-change.rationale: Calls for disruption and risk and welcomed Trump as disruption to a stagnant order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His Free Forever PAC backed candidates for stricter border control and restrictive immigration policy, although he is himself an immigrant.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Argues one-world governance for existential risks is going from the frying pan into the fire and links it to the Antichrist.

free-trade.rationale: Attacked free-trade ideology in 2019 as an obstacle to being tough on China, and in 2026 criticised Western parties for exchanging industrial jobs for cheap Chinese imports.

nation-first.rationale: At NatCon 2019 he said decisions should be run through the test of whether a policy is good for the United States rather than for humanity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Condemns the Libya intervention and Afghan nation-building as built on lies, and urged an end to stupid wars.

open-borders.rationale: His PAC supported stricter border control and restrictive immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Argues the stagnation since the 1970s is the problem, and calls a degrowth society super oppressive.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Says he is not a crazy environmentalist, treats environmentalism as a route to one-world totalitarianism, and compared the invocation of climate science to a poker tell of exaggeration.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Warns against technological utopianism (technology will not by itself guarantee freedom) while treating technology as the main escape from politics; calls AI more than a nothing burger but less than total transformation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Lists deregulating nuclear power and building new or better reactors, even fusion, as the direction he wants.

experts-over-public.rationale: Attacks expert consensus on COVID, the Fed and Afghanistan as dogmatic epistemic closure, while also distrusting crowds.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: At NatCon 2019 he proposed 25 percent tariffs on China as a starting point; in 2026 he criticised trading local industrial jobs for cheap Chinese goods.

one-party-rule.rationale: Calls Chinese party rule totalitarian and a 'horrible society' and says he stands against totalitarian collectives.

democracy-best.rationale: Wrote that he no longer believes freedom and democracy are compatible and later said majority-rule conceits should be doubted.

military-superiority.rationale: Complained that US bases run on floppy disks and jets cannot fly in rain, and in 2026 feared the US would not defend against China over Taiwan.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: His stagnation thesis treats the loss of industrial and scientific dynamism as the central failure, and he praises 1890-1970 progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Says society should take a lot more risk, still believes in trying AI, and sees stagnation as the central danger.

human-enhancement.rationale: Lead funder of the Enhanced Games, which allow performance-enhancing substances, and a long-time funder of life-extension and transhumanist projects.

restore-past-order.rationale: Told the RNC that Make America Great Again is not a return to the past but a path to a brighter future.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Says he prefers concrete particulars to abstractions and refuses simple historical templates for China.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Argues freedom lies in escape from politics and funded seasteading as a way to create new space for exit and experiment.

state-as-business.rationale: Backs competing, semi-autonomous jurisdictions (seasteading, charter cities) and demands that government meet Silicon Valley standards of competence.

total-state.rationale: Stands against totalitarian collectives and describes the Chinese and Leninist model as the 'big eye of Sauron'.

national-rebirth.rationale: Describes a long national decline and calls on the country to rebuild and go back to a high-tech future.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Warned that enormous deficits and money printing were setting up inflation and that the 2021 policy mix violated economics; criticised Reagan-style borrowing.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Is a self-described Orthodox Christian who contrasts the skepticism of revelation with reason's trust in crowds.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says the economy is broken and government failed (RNC 2016), that politicians tell the biggest lies, and that elites are caught in epistemic closure.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Says competition makes people fixate on rivals and lose sight of building something new; progress comes from one-of-a-kind creation.

party-controls-media.rationale: Fought campus speech codes as a student and argues that being unable to say something suggests it is true.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Criticises collectivism and conformity, calls the near-unanimity of academia a gentle version of North Korea, and funds dropouts through his fellowship.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Criticises 'peace and safetyism' and says society should take far more risk, including in medicine.

space-expansion.rationale: Urged redoubling efforts to commercialise space and contrasts a lost Mars ambition with the Middle East wars.

ban-cartels.rationale: Argues every entrepreneur should aim at a monopoly and that dynamic monopolies are good for society; criticises only static, rent-collecting ones.

no-bailouts.rationale: Lists being forced to bail out reckless financial companies among the rights violations of the day and blames government moral hazard for the 2008 crisis.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Argued libertarians should escape politics and called politics toxic, but he has also funded candidates repeatedly.

defeat-communism.rationale: Warns that a second Cold War with China could end in an unjust peace and wants the West to resist.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Openly gay, funds gay-rights causes and told the RNC he is proud to be gay.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Argues every society needs dissent and heterodox views and criticises the Chinese party-state's silencing.

property-franchise.rationale: Said no class of people should be disenfranchised.

racial-franchise.rationale: Said no class of people should be disenfranchised.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Argues that nonstop talk of existential risk is what an Antichrist-like one-world regulator would use, while saying the human race should survive.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Frames environmentalism, regulation and global governance as markers of an end-times struggle with the Antichrist.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Describes PayPal's founding aim as a world currency free from government control and his fund bought bitcoin; no explicit statement on tracing or blocking payments.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Said student debt should not be socialised; instead make it dischargeable in bankruptcy with the college that gave a bad education bearing the loss.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Frames the Judeo-Christian impulse as transcending nature and favours transforming the mortal body, though he says he would rather keep his body than upload.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Describes green politics as the strongest force pulling Europe toward an oppressive future and rejects degrowth.

women-suffrage.rationale: Wrote that he does not think any class of people should be disenfranchised and called it absurd to suggest taking away women's votes.

close-ties-china.rationale: Urged tariffs and punishment of firms doing business in China and calls China a totalitarian threat.

notes: Views changed over time: a libertarian (Ron Paul donor, Cato 2009) who by 2016-2019 backed Trump and national conservatism; in 2023-2025 he stepped back from donations and was critical of Trump's distractions. Recent positions are used where they differ. His own full texts for Straussian Moment, Zero to One and the 2019 NYT op-ed could not be fetched, so economics, healthcare, guns, abortion and similar issues are left null. The Reason account of the 2019 NatCon speech is a critical secondary source used only for reported content, and the Le Grand Continent text is a French translation of his 2026 handout.
